subject.title: [codex] fix(sessions): report archive cleanup in sessions cleanup

question: Should `sessions cleanup --enforce` physically remove stale `.deleted.*` and `.reset.*` archive files according to existing retention rules and report that in dry-run/apply output?
rationale: The patch is a narrow implementation, but the behavior intentionally changes retained session artifacts on disk and overlaps with unresolved retention-policy reports.

options.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
options.body: Land the PR as the narrow #75658 fix and keep broader archive naming/no-delete and sidecar cleanup decisions on separate issues.

options.title: Require broader artifact policy first
options.body: Hold the PR until maintainers decide whether deleted/reset archives should be hard-deleted, renamed, moved, compressed, or preserved.

options.title: Close as wrong direction
options.body: Reject physical archive deletion from `sessions cleanup` and route disk-bloat mitigation toward non-destructive archive storage instead.

recommendation.title: Accept archive-retention cleanup
recommendation.body: Land the PR as the narrow #75658 fix and keep broader archive naming/no-delete and sidecar cleanup decisions on separate issues.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice is closest to the original sessions cleanup command and maintenance UX ownership trail.
